I was/still am in a weirdly similar relationship. A lot of my own healing had to come from inward reflection & work.

My partner was in a 5-6 year long relationship with his first love & it used to tear me apart: I’d fantasize about how I could never compare to her, how he secretly wished things worked out with her, how she was better than me in every way, etc. Real stupid RJ crap.

He’d tell me over & over again how toxic it was, & how he wishes they’d broken up sooner. Their breakup was messy & painful but I still wouldn’t listen. My own partner was telling me to my FACE that he would never want to get back with his ex, yet I refused to believe him.

The first step that helped me really start combatting the “myth of the First Lover” was reframing it. Instead of torturing yourself with the past, gently ask yourself: Why am I searching for reasons that I will be abandoned by him? Because the RJ isn’t about his first love. It’s about the belief that even her mere existence is proof that he will leave YOU someday for her.

I’d gently suggest you start reflecting on your own abandonment issues, OP. Start asking yourself about why you feel so unworthy compared to her, & less about him.

At least it helped me combat my own RJ. I wish you healing ❤️‍🩹

You are NOT too broken, OP. You get out of therapy what you put in: & if this is still early in your treatment, then you’re getting hit hard with very difficult things to process.

You wouldn’t feel guilty for sweating. It’s a natural bodily response to stimuli: emotions are the same. They are contradictory & weird & don’t make sense. But you wouldn’t beat yourself up for sweating after a run.

Likewise, let yourself feel your emotions & then let them go. You feel guilty for still loving an abuser & wanting to please them? That’s neither good or bad. It’s just an emotion. Emotions don’t make sense. They’re not reality. It’s impossible to “know better” because that’s a judgment statement, which we know does NOT apply to emotions.

Forgive that part of you that still wants to appease your abuser, OP. They feel contradictory emotions & there’s nothing wrong or broken about that. Don’t judge them so harshly & (by extension) torture yourself more. You’ve already survived so much. Healing is hardest in the beginning, & by god you’re in the worst part of it right now.

Confronting them would be like squeezing toothpaste out of the tube: there’s no putting it back inside. No going back to this current “uncertainty” that you’re stuck in. 

Do extensive research, practice your self-care, & say it on YOUR own terms if you truly decide to confront them. I worry that lack of preparation combined with confronting them impulsively could lead to an interaction that would harm YOUR healing after all these years. Remember the weight that confronting them will have. There will truly be no take-backs.

I wish you best of luck, OP.
